fam_f0002: No intermediate amount is rounded: each year's depreciation charge and year-end book value are carried forward at full Decimal precision (50 significant digits), not to cents.
The DDB rate is the exact fraction 2/useful life (for example 2/11), never a rounded decimal.
Each year's declining-balance charge is beginning book value x 2/useful life, computed at 50 significant digits without rounding.
Each year's straight-line charge is (beginning book value - salvage) / remaining years, computed at 50 significant digits without rounding; if book value is below salvage the base is zero.
Remaining years for year y (1-based) equals useful life - y + 1, so year 1 uses the full useful life and the current year is included in the count.
Each year the depreciation charge is the larger of the declining-balance charge and the straight-line charge, so the switch is tested every year rather than made once.
Each year's charge is capped at (beginning book value - salvage), with that headroom floored at zero, so year-end book value never falls below salvage.
The simulation runs years 1 through min(elapsed years, useful life) inclusive, and the elapsed-year book value is the year-end book value of the last simulated year.
If elapsed years exceed the useful life, the book value is set to salvage value.
The only rounding in the program is the final step: the unrounded book value is quantized to two decimal places (cents) using round-half-up.
The final output is the rounded dollar amount in cents followed by the text ' $' (for example '76109.31 $'), with no thousands separator.
fam_f0004: No rounding is applied anywhere in the code: the returned pressure in bar is the full-precision Decimal quotient, not rounded to any number of decimal places or significant figures.
Each intermediate (volume in m3, moles, kelvin, pascals) is passed along as its full-precision Decimal string with no rounding.
The ideal gas pressure is p = (n x R x T) / V, computed as n x R x T first and then divided by V, in the default Decimal context of 28 significant digits.
R is the literal value 8.314462618 J/(K mol), used exactly as written with no truncation or rounding.
Pascals are converted to bar by dividing by exactly 100000 at 60-digit precision, so the bar result is not rounded.
Kelvin input is used as given; Celsius adds exactly 273.15; Fahrenheit computes (F - 32) x 5 / 9 and then adds 273.15, all at 60-digit precision.
A temperature is rejected unless the converted kelvin value is strictly greater than 0.
Volume unit factors to m3: m3 = 1; dm3, l, litre(s), liter(s) = 1E-3; cm3, cc, ml, millilitre(s), milliliter(s) = 1E-6; mm3 = 1E-9; unit text is matched after removing whitespace and '^', lowercased.
A volume is rejected unless it is strictly greater than 0.
Amount factors to mol: mol, mole, moles = 1; mmol = 1E-3; kmol = 1E3; an amount of zero is accepted (only negative amounts are rejected).
A trailing 'k' not followed by a letter multiplies the number by 1000; the words thousand, million, billion and bn multiply by 10^3, 10^6, 10^9 respectively.
Comma-separated digit groups in a quantity are read as thousands separators and the commas are removed before conversion.
The pressure in pascals must be finite and non-negative before conversion to bar.
